headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared file-reading and broad egress; no direct write-conflict is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and files from supported macOS apps, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and can use web search. If Khoj content is fed into ChatGPT or vice versa through shared files, either agent may treat attacker-controlled text as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible in default use, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF the user places untrusted text into shared files or notes that both agents read
IF either agent is prompted to follow instructions embedded in retrieved content
mitigations: Separate the agents' input folders
Strip instructions from retrieved notes before reuse
Use a human review step for any copied content
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between retrieval and generation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read files, and ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code while Khoj indexes personal notes/documents. That creates a default pathway for sensitive data to flow into both systems, with ChatGPT sending requests to api.openai.com and Khoj using cloud or configured search providers. The shared-data blast radius can include multiple work products.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is indexed in Khoj and uploaded or opened in ChatGPT Desktop
IF either agent is connected to external APIs while handling that document
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared indexes
Use separate accounts or workspaces
Review API/data-sharing settings in both tools
Redact secrets before upload or indexing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem or modify git state, so direct write-write conflict is blocked. The remaining overlap is read-only filesystem access and broad/vendor egress, which can still cause coordination friction but not the high-severity mutable-resource collision described in the rubric.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared workspaces
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Use file locks if write access is added
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat system that can surface indexed notes, and ChatGPT Desktop can consume files and app context. If one agent's output is copied into the other without verification, errors can cascade from retrieval into generated answers or actions. The pair does not show explicit action-taking authority, so this is below high, but the default handoff remains risky.
conditions: IF output from Khoj is pasted into ChatGPT Desktop as authoritative context
IF ChatGPT-generated text is re-indexed into Khoj without verification
mitigations: Require source links for copied claims
Verify retrieved facts before reuse
Mark AI-generated notes as untrusted
Use a second-pass human review for actions
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state residency, retention, or certification alignment. ChatGPT Desktop sends data to api.openai.com, while Khoj may use a cloud or self-hosted server and configured search providers. Because compliance posture is undocumented and could diverge on the same data class, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound data is processed by both agents
IF one deployment is cloud-hosted while the other is self-hosted or routed through third-party providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document residency and retention settings
Use separate environments for regulated and general data
Review vendor DPAs and logging settings
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems
